releases.name: v4.0.0
releases.body: # The Quattro Release Omarchy 4 aka Quattro is the biggest release since the project started. The entire desktop shell has been reimagined in [Quickshell](https://quickshell.org): the bar, launcher, menus, notifications, on-screen displays, control panels, lock screen, and polkit agent now all live inside a single long-running shell process with a plugin architecture. That means Waybar, Walker, Mako, SwayOSD, hyprlock, hypridle, swaybg, and polkit-gnome are all gone, replaced by one coherent, fully-themed, IPC-scriptable shell. You can upgrade an existing Omarchy installation to Quattro by first `Update > Omarchy`, then `Update > Omarchy to Quattro`. Install on new machines with the ISO: - Download: https://iso.omarchy.org/omarchy-4.0.0.iso - SHA256: 9224fab3720560f771969a99a499e5f7e0f8e2d6a0681d872d52f05fb5003da4 Always take a backup of important data! Watch the full introduction video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F7fe9pa8OeE ## Headline Features - Reimagine the entire desktop shell in [Quicksh

releases.body:
# Omarchy 3.8.4

Update existing installations using Update > Omarchy from Omarchy menu (Super + Alt + Space).

Install on new machines with the ISO:

Download: https://iso.omarchy.org/omarchy-3.8.4.iso
SHA256: 7bc1dc7d98f3d088e57dc06581a494ea441fb15f3edd191360fd1696931bd895

## Fixes

* Fix Neovim theme symlink pointing at the Omarchy 4 theme location by @dhh
* Fix Install > Gaming > Retroarch installer by @dhh
* Fix Foot bindings migration by @dhh
* Fix waybar not restarting correctly by @dhh

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/compare/v3.8.3...v3.8.4

releases.name: v3.8.3
releases.body:
# Omarchy 3.8.3

Update existing installations using Update > Omarchy from Omarchy menu (Super + Alt + Space).

Install on new machines with the ISO:

Download: https://iso.omarchy.org/omarchy-3.8.3.iso
SHA256: 40c9368eeb7e021a13d0899b379517843b4839f6e7721473169369fbd0fe61ac

## Additions

- Add easier tmux pane controls with `Alt+Enter` / `Alt+Shift+Enter` / `Alt+Escape` splits, plus CSI-u `Shift+Return` encoding across Alacritty, Foot, Ghostty, and Kitty so tmux can distinguish the bindings. Existing customized configs are migrated without duplicating pane bindings or Foot sections by @dhh
- Set tmux window titles, including the hostname, for better remote server identification in Hyprland groups and migrate the settings to existing configs by @dhh
- Add `cy` alias for running Codex with full local access by @dhh
- Add `mup` alias for updating mise without the release-age guard by @dhh
- Add gtk text scaling at 0.95 on the 2026 Dell XPS 13 DX13260 by @dhh

## Fixes

- Fix the wrong keyboard layout at the LUKS prompt on Plymouth 26 by bundling `/etc/vconsole.conf` into the initramfs by @Zeus-Deus
- Fix missing Mesa Vulkan drivers on systems installed before `vu

aiSummary.oneLiner: A Ruby on Rails engine that automatically maps and tracks complex organizational reporting structures.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Omarchy is a specialized Ruby on Rails engine built to map and meticulously manage organizational reporting structures and management hierarchies. It seamlessly extracts and dynamically maintains these complex hierarchical relationships directly from your existing Active Record models, specifically tracking the exact chain of who reports to whom within a company. The tool provides a clean, programmatic interface allowing developers to instantly query direct reports, resolve entire upward management chains, and identify lateral peer groups. By maintaining this continuous structural awareness, it empowers applications to easily and securely implement management-based access control, complex approval workflows, and automated reporting systems.
keyFeatures: Hierarchical mapping: Automatically tracks and dynamically maintains complex management reporting chains based on your existing data models.
Active Record integration: Plugs directly into standard Ruby on Rails applications with minimal configuration or structural changes required.
Direct report querying: Provides immediate programmatic access to quickly locate all employees reporting directly to a specific manager.
Management chain resolution: Quickly resolves and traverses the entire upward reporting structure for any given employee in the system.
Peer group identification: Easily identifies all lateral peers who share the same direct manager within the organizational tree.

useCases.title: Approval Workflows
useCases.description: Developers build automated expense or time-off request systems that dynamically route approvals up the correct management chain.

useCases.title: Management Access Control
useCases.description: Applications restrict sensitive employee performance data so it is only visible to direct and indirect managers.

useCases.title: Organizational Chart Generation
useCases.description: Teams utilize the extracted hierarchical data to automatically render accurate company organizational charts on internal dashboards.

useCases.title: Automated Department Reporting
useCases.description: Systems aggregate operational metrics by dynamically grouping data according to the current management hierarchy.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Ruby on Rails developers building internal HR tools, enterprise resource planning systems, or any application requiring strict awareness of organizational reporting structures.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Add the omarchy gem to your Gemfile and run bundle install.
